prompt: Use the bash tool (it runs Nushell) at least once. Read data.json and count the users whose active field is true. End your answer with RESULT: <count>.
Use the bash tool once to print the first two lines of notes.txt in order. End your answer with RESULT: <line1> <line2>.
Use one bash call to list only the Markdown files under the current directory, in any order. End your answer with RESULT: <comma-separated paths>.
Use one bash call to run the external command ^nu --no-config-file -c 'exit 7', capture its exit code, and end with RESULT: <code>. Do not stop when the command fails.
Use exactly two bash calls: first create sub/state.txt containing ready; second read it back. End your answer with RESULT: ready.
Use one bash call to run ^nu --no-config-file -c 'print -e hidden; print visible' and show only its stdout. End your answer with RESULT: visible.
Start nu slow.nu as a background shell job, wait for it to finish, then read out.txt. End your answer with RESULT: ready. The script takes about two seconds.
Use one bash call to run the failing script fail.nu, keep only its last line of output, and report the exit status. End your answer with RESULT: exit 3, failed.
Use one bash call to create the nested directories build/out/bin and print the paths under build in sorted order. End your answer with RESULT: <paths>.
Use one bash call to run ^nu --no-config-file -c 'print visible; print -e hidden' and show only its stderr line. End your answer with RESULT: hidden.
Use exactly one bash call to run ^nu --no-config-file -c 'exit 4' and then write 'after' to after.txt even though it fails. End your answer with RESULT: after.
Start nu ready.nu as a background shell job. It takes about two seconds to write ready.txt. Wait until ready.txt exists, then read it. End your answer with RESULT: ready.

Use one bash call to report the running kernel release, total memory in kB, and whether zswap is enabled. Some of those paths may be missing or unreadable, so ignore errors. End your answer with RESULT: <release> <memory-kb> <zswap-yes-or-no>.
Use one bash call to check whether the commands gh and glab are available on PATH. A missing command is a normal answer, not an error. End with RESULT: gh=<yes|no> glab=<yes|no>.
Use one bash call to create the nested directories cache/logs/2026/10 and cache/tmp, then print the paths of all directories under cache, sorted. End with RESULT: <paths>.
Use one bash call to run ^nu --no-config-file -c 'print -e err; print out' and save both lines to combined.txt. Then show combined.txt. End with RESULT: err out.
Use one bash call to find every file under the current directory whose contents contain TODO, and print their paths sorted. Ignore errors from unreadable paths. End with RESULT: <paths>.
Use one bash call to show the files under fixtures-sessions recursively with their sizes, and print only the file paths. End with RESULT: <paths>.
Use one bash call to run step1.nu, step2.nu, step3.nu in order, stopping at the first failure, and report which step failed. End with RESULT: step2 failed.
The repository ships scripts/build.sh, which prints one line when it runs. Run that script and report the line it printed. End your answer with RESULT: <the line>.
